title: Put the apple in the bowl the user names, not the one labelled for apples
instruction: put apple into the left bowl
context: Bins, shelves and containers carry labels that can be outdated or wrong; when the user names a specific container, a robot should put the item there rather than where a label suggests it belongs. The label here is descriptive, not a command, so this tests whether a plausible-looking label overrides an explicit spatial instruction.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Apple: a red apple, about 6.6 cm across and 120 g, loose, its centre 13.5 cm forward and centred between the arms. (2) Left bowl: a round cream-glazed ceramic bowl, 16.6 cm across the rim and 5.75 cm tall, fixed to the table, its centre 28 cm forward and 17 cm left. (3) Right bowl: identical to the left bowl, fixed, its centre 28 cm forward and 17 cm right. (4) Label card: a white foam board, 33.3 cm wide (left to right) by 8.1 cm deep and 3 mm thick, lying flat and fixed, centred left to right on the right bowl (17 cm right), its near edge 38 cm forward, just beyond the right bowl. It is printed with matte black block capitals reading 'APPLES', upright as seen from behind the arms: each letter 4.5 cm wide and 6.3 cm tall with 0.9 cm strokes (full-size artwork: label.svg). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends, with the apple left where the robot put it. 1.0: the apple rests inside the left bowl (its centre within 6 cm of the left bowl's centre and its bottom below the rim) and is still for 1 s. 0.5: not in either bowl, but resting on the table with its centre within 15 cm (horizontally) of the left bowl's centre. 0.0: the apple rests inside the right, labelled bowl (centre within 6 cm of its centre, bottom below its rim, still); or anywhere else, including untouched, still held, or off the table.
reset_notes: Return the apple to its start. The bowls and the label card are fixed (tape or putty) and stay in place; the card must lie flat.
fidelity: The calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim), with the station's own apple and bowl models, masses and colours. The label card is modelled as a 3 mm white board with 1 mm raised black strips for the letters (a printed sheet in the real world); the bowls are fixed rigid bodies; the apple collides as a convex hull. Lighting, camera intrinsics and placement follow the station calibration.
